name: ABBOTSFORD (Stoney Creek)
map_popup_text:
ABBOTSFORD (Stoney Creek)
Spill
ABBOTSFORD – Chemical Spill at Stoney Creek July 3
Firefighting foam escaped from a disconnected hose and entered the storm drain and subsequently the waterway. July 8 UPDATE: Representatives from Semá:th First Nation, Stó:lō
Guardians, Lower Fraser Fisheries Alliance and environmental consultants GHD removed 1,048 deceased fish and relocated 1,198 fish to fresh water. Quantum Murray Environmental established a water treatment system that channels contaminated water through a treatment process and returns it to the creek. To date, more than 211,000 gallons of water has been treated.
7/3/2024

map_popup_text:

Do Not Consume Advisory
29/MAY/2017 - BRENT KENNEDY ELEMENTARY SCHOOL WS, 1092 Hwy 6
DNC issued: Untreated drinking water at risk of containing pathogens. INH
17/JAN/2023 – In the News: Brent Kennedy Elementary has relied on bottled water since Interior Health issued a do not drink order due to unsafe iron and manganese levels.
In the years since the order, efforts have been made to resolve this
alternative sources revealed the same issues of unsafe iron and manganese levels
new treatment plant has operational issues due to scale deposits of iron and manganese
the system is also challenged by unstable chlorine levels resulting from the systems non-use over weekends and holidays.
A spokesperson for Interior Health said there is no timeline for lifting the drinking ban, but superintendent Trish Smillie told the Nelson Star she believes the water quality will be approved in the near future.

name: DAWSON CREEK
map_popup_text:
DAWSON CREEK
Severe Water Shortage
State-of-Emergency has been renewed to January 20, 2026. Kiskatinaw River, the communitys water source, is at record-low levels, posing a risk of the river freezing solid. This Water System supplies about 15,000 people in the City and surrounding rural residents, including the Village of Pouce Coupe.
October 14, 2025 State-of-Emergency declared due to ongoing water crisis, a severe and prolonged drought that has significantly reduced the communitys available water supply despite years of conservation, careful management, and investment in water infrastructure. Stage 3 Water Conservation Measures have been in place since September.
The City is currently seeking approval to construct a new intake system on the Peace River and a 52-kilometre transmission pipeline running from Taylor to Dawson Creek, complete with pumping stations to move water through the system. Tapping into groundwater aquifers became an “unviable option” when the supply was found to be brackish, containing a salinity level of 0.5g and 3.0g of salt per litre, therefore not suitable for potable water.

name: GRANISLE
map_popup_text:
GRANISLE
Do Not Consume Advisory
GRANISLE COMMUNITY WS –
JANUARY 6, 2026 - DNC remains in effect. The community waits for an engineering assessment, conducted in collaboration with the manufacturer, of their Water Treatment Plants chemical and mechanical issues.
DECEMBER 14, 2025 - DNC issued due to a coagulant leak from the treatment system. The coagulant, composed of aluminum chlorohydrate, is used to bind materials in the raw source water facilitating the filtration process. Recent testing of treated water supply showed ALUMINUM at 3.75 mg/L, the maximum acceptable concentration is 2.9 mg/L.
SEPTEMBER 04, 2025 - WQA issued due to mechanical issues with the filtration system and elevated turbidity.
As a precautionary measure, people with weakened or undeveloped immune systems may wish to boil water for at least one minute, use bottled water, or use an alternative approved source of water. Elderly people, pregnant women, children under the age of two, people with AIDS, cancer, diabetes or kidney disease and people being treated with immuno-suppressing medications should take appropriate measures.

Water Quality Advisory
WQA in effect February 25. Vancouver Coastal Health has applied a Permanent Water Quality Advisory to BC Parks hand-pump systems due to the inherent microbiological risk associated with untreated groundwater at publicly accessible sources.
Advisory documentation identified potential contamination pathways from backflow, nearby sources such as outhouses, campsites, vehicles, campfires, fuel storage, greywater discharge, blackwater holding tanks, and inadequate grading or drainage around the wellhead that may allow surface water infiltration.

name: KERSLEY
map_popup_text:
KERSLEY
Boil Water Advisory
ALAMO MOTEL & RV WS –
BWN issued November 30 due to recent sampling history that shows recurring overgrown of background colonies.
The water is supplied from a shallow well, which is subject to microbiological contamination. The last inspection dated May 2024 revealed that the Treatment System does not meet the Drinking Water Treatment Objectives (Microbiological) for Ground Water Supplies
Chlorination is done manually once every week.
In-order to rescind the Boil Water Notice, Northern Health has instructed the Operator to hire a treatment specialist to assess the Water System and propose an effective Treatment System that meets the BC Drinking Water Treatment Objectives.

A Water Quality Advisory (WQA) was issued in February 2020. The primary function of the WQA is to notify water system users of the protozoan parasite risk from surface water supplies. It is recognized that due to lack of available power supply options, adding a second form of disinfection to the surface water source is logistically very difficult. The source of electrical energy is solar panels to battery storage.

name: OLALLA Water System
map_popup_text:
OLALLA Water System
Water Quality Advisory
MARCH 11, 2025 - WQA remains in effect along with chlorination of the system.
JANUARY 20, 2026 - WQA remains in effect along with chlorination of the system.
NOVEMBER 6, 2025 WQA in effect.
Based on recent bacteriological results, the Regional District of Okanagan-Similkameen (RDOS), in consultation with Interior Health, have downgraded the Boil Water Notice (BWN) that has been in effect since April 24, 2025. Total coliforms and background bacteria have been periodically reported since August 2024
the BWN was the result of an increase in the frequency and quantity being reported.
The source of the contamination has yet to be determined in spite the substantial testing completed by the RDOS. As a result, the System will remain chlorinated for the foreseeable future.
Currently, there is no treatment system in place for the groundwater (a single deep well), supplying the Water System. Typically, the System is monitored for potential contamination and undergoes periodic flushes and temporary chlorination as needed. This System serves approximately 250 connections. --
AUGUST 11, 2025 BWN remains in effect.
This System remains under a Boil Water Notice as Regional District of Okanagan-Similkameen (RDOS) has yet to determine the source of contamination, despite their continued efforts. Most recent efforts involved:
• The Reservoir was isolated, and the System was ran dynamically for the last few weeks.
• The Reservoir was also emptied and disinfected while offline.
• Further work to improve the water quality is anticipated to take place in the fall.
• Additional measures will be implemented in the coming months to prevent backflow conditions within the System, and the reservoir is expected to be lined for further source protection. --
JUNE 27, 2025 BWN remains in effect and Temporary Chlorination has been reinstated. In continued efforts to determine the source of the contamination RDOS is now planning to change the configuration of the system and informs residents that the chlorination will be turned on and off for different periods of time. --
JUNE 9, 2025 BWN remains in effect and Temporary Chlorination will be suspended to facilitate further bacteriological testing as part of on-going efforts to pinpoint the source of the contamination.
Total coliforms and background bacteria have been periodically reported in water system samples since August 2024. The most recent BWN (issued April 24) is the result of an increase in the frequency and quantity being reported.
In the report dated May 23, Total Coliform bacteria are present throughout the Distribution System, including the Storage Reservoir and No Total Coliform bacteria were reported from the source well. Based on the level of bacteria reported, the RDOS decided to reinstate the temporary chlorination.
RDOS on-going efforts to determine the source of the contamination entering the system include:
• Enhanced bacteriological sampling,
• Extensive flushing of the distribution system,
• Temporary chlorination (October 11, 2024 to February 18, 2025),
• WQA (March 13 to 24),
• BWN ISSUED APRIL 24, 2025,
• Temporary chlorination (April 30 to May 9),
• May 2, 2025, the RDOS hired a contractor with a Remotely Operated Vehicle (ROV) to inspect the inside of the storage Reservoir, and no apparent sources of contamination were noted from this inspection.
• Temporary chlorination (May 23, 2025 to June 9, 2025),
RDOS is now planning to isolate the storage Reservoir from the distribution system to further determine if the source of contamination is associated with the Reservoir. This will require some additional programming of the pump control system in advance to allow the system to modulate the speed of the Well Pump to continually maintain a set pressure in the distribution system while the Reservoir is isolated. Once this programming is complete, chlorination will again be removed from the system (scheduled for June 9) to allow for bacteriological testing.
The Olalla System consists of a single deep source groundwater well, an elevated storage reservoir and distribution system. The water supply is typically not treated
the system is monitored for potential contamination and undergoes periodic flushes and temporary chlorination as needed. This System has approx. 200 service connections.

name: QUAMICHAN LAKE
map_popup_text:
QUAMICHAN LAKE
Water Quality Advisory
QUAMICHAN LAKE (North Cowichan) – (WQA/BGA) June 27 Permanent Advisory has been in place for 10 years as a result of ongoing high bacteriological counts and frequent toxic algae blooms.
Quamichan Lake has been subject to cyanobacteria (blue-green algae) since the 1930s. In the past two decades, the blooms have become longer and more intense. The root cause of these blooms is high concentration of phosphorus, which is largely due to excessive nutrient loading that has accumulated in the lake sediment over 150 years of runoff from forested, farmed and developed lands in the Quamichan watershed.
Human activity since the turn of the last century has elevated nutrient levels in Quamichan Lake such that it is now considered a Highly Eutrophic Lake
dissolved oxygen has depleted to the point where the aquatic life begins to die off. Due to this predisposition, Island Health no longer tests the water and has a permanent advisory in place.

map_popup_text:
SOUTH HAZELTON
Water Quality Advisory
SOUTH HAZELTON COMMUNITY WS – WQA issued March 12 due to water reservoirs being taken offline to complete necessary maintenance and cleaning from March 12 to March 20.
As a result of this work, higher turbidity levels may occur. High turbidity can make it easier for microorganisms to remain present in the water. While the water is still considered safe for most users, people with weakened or undeveloped immune systems (e.g. elderly people, pregnant women, children under the age of two, people with AIDS, cancer, diabetes or kidney disease, people being treated with immuno-suppressing medications) may wish to take extra precautions, such as: 1) boil water for at least one minute and let it cool before using\, 2) use bottled water, or 3) use an alternative approved source of water.

name: YOHO NATIONAL PARK
map_popup_text:
YOHO NATIONAL PARK
Boil Water Advisory
BWA in effect.
Potable water is available in each of Yoho National Parks four campgrounds.
Water from creeks, streams or lakes must be treated or brought to a rolling boil for a minimum of 2 minutes before drinking.
27/MAR/2024 - Parks Canada announces long-term water closure due to invasive parasite.
Fishing, swimming, wading, the use of any watercraft such as a boat, paddle board, raft, or any other vessel in the area will be prohibited for at least a year.
26/OCT/2023 – Positive detection of whirling disease
caused by an invasive, parasitic myxosporean called Myxobolus Cerebralis.
